title: Master job queue
notes: Jobs carry a type and a callback. `iolink_main` switches on `job->type`; every case except `PD_EVENT` and `EXIT` runs `job->callback`, and the dispatcher connection `job.dispatch` confirms every case there. The CM and ODE wrappers pass the type through a parameter, so their callers are matched too; the sites inside the wrappers are forwarding sites. `job->type = …` in `iolink_main.c` covers the jobs posted without the helper; `keys` keeps `PD_EVENT` and `EXIT` and drops the resets to `IOLINK_JOB_NONE` and the helper's own `job->type = type`.

title: Mailbox
notes: The master has three mailboxes: `mbox` for submitted jobs (fetched by `iolink_main`), and the free-job pools `mbox_avail` and `mbox_api_avail` (`iolink_main` returns finished jobs to them; `iolink_fetch_avail_job`, `iolink_fetch_avail_api_job` and `iolink_post_job_pd_event` take jobs from them). The handle is written `master->mbox_avail` in one place and `port->master->mbox_avail` in another, so `keyMember` keys each site by the member name; each of the three names belongs to one mailbox.

title: DL thread event
notes: `dl_main` waits on `dl->event` and tests each flag; the dispatcher connection `dl-event.dispatch` confirms the flags tested there. Limited to the stack; the sample application uses `os_event_set` for its own events.
